core_obligations: Present the base as a cofiltered limit (proof lines 16551-16560): K being separably closed, the scheme Spec(K) x_S Spec(O^sh_{S,s}) is the spectrum of a filtered colimit of etale K-algebras, each of which is a finite product of copies of K, so it is a cofiltered limit of disjoint unions of copies of Spec(K) indexed by nonempty finite sets A_i.

Rewrite the compared scheme (proof lines 16561-16572): substituting this presentation into Spec(O^sh_{X,x}) x_S Spec(K) and using the defining fibre product identity expresses the scheme as the corresponding cofiltered limit of the terms Spec(O^sh_{X,x}) x_{Spec(O^sh_{S,s})} Spec(K).
Conclude (proof lines 16573-16579): since cohomology in this setting commutes with such limits by the colimit theorem, the equality in condition (1) is equivalent to the equality in condition (2).
proof_roadmap: Use separably closedness of K to write the base change of the strict henselisation as a cofiltered limit of disjoint unions of copies of Spec(K).
Identify the fibre product in condition (1) as the same limit of the fibre products appearing in condition (2).
Apply the colimit theorem to turn the resulting identity of cohomologies into the equivalence of the two conditions.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that two natural formulations of the stalk comparison over the strict henselisations are equivalent (statement lines 16531-16548). The proof (proof lines 16550-16579) is a limit computation: separably closedness of K presents the relevant base change as a cofiltered limit of disjoint unions of copies of Spec(K), the compared fibre product is rewritten as the limit of the local fibre products, and the colimit theorem for cohomology of such limits finishes. H2: one limit presentation and one application of the colimit theorem.
